# Brain Paper — Research Coordination

## Project Context
Mouse widefield closed-loop PI controller vs open-loop analysis.
Controller uses kernel average of a cortical region as output; PI controller drives input.
Two mice: AL_0033 (9 sessions), AL_0039 (4 sessions) = 13 controller sessions, Jan–Apr 2025. (Verified 2026-06-16 from loaded cache m1–m13.)

**Core question:** Does the closed-loop controller reduce neural variability and error compared to open-loop?
**Secondary questions:** Do motion, frequency-band power, and wide-brain activity explain trial-to-trial variability? Do these differ between OL and CL?

**For tasks and priorities → `TASKS.md`**
**For completed findings and paper claims → `FINDINGS.md`**
**For meeting decisions → `MEETINGS.md`**

## Change Log

### 2026-08-12 — 🔴 `dev_metric='cperr'` SILENTLY FALLS BACK to peakdev: paper panel 2F is labelled "Prediction error" but plots |Peak dev|
**Changed/Found:** `motion_analysis.m` and `prestim_variance.m` both default to `dev_metric='cperr'`, guarded per-amp by `strcmp(dev_metric,'cperr') && isfield(imp_e,'cp_err') && ~isempty(...)`. **`imp.cp_err` is never produced anywhere in the repo** — a full-repo grep finds only consumption sites in these two scripts (plus an unrelated `utils/cp_error_heatmap.m`), and `allExperiments(k).imp` carries `Peak_imp / Peak_imp_dev / Peak_imp_mean` but no `cp_err`. It is created only by `contra_prediction.m`, which a plain `load_experiments` run never invokes. So the guard fails and every plot falls through to `Peak_imp_dev` — while `dev_tag` stays `'cperr'` and `dev_ylabel` stays `'Prediction error'` (that label is only corrected when `dev_metric=='peakdev'`).
**Evidence:** `prevar_vs_dev_allamps_motexcl_{,cperr_,peakdev_}AL_0033_2025-01-29_en1.pdf` are all exactly **23807 bytes** (different MD5 only because PDFs embed a creation timestamp) — three filenames, one plot. `imp_motion_devscatter_all_sessions_cperr.pdf` (panel **2F**, an ACTIVE Fig-2 paper panel per PAPER.md line 93) was regenerated today 15:10 under the mislabel. Supplementary `imp_motion_devscatter_cperr_*.png` likewise.
**Fixed:** added a loud fallback guard to both scripts — if no session carries `imp.cp_err`, warn and set `dev_metric`/`dev_tag` to `'peakdev'` so the axis label and filename match what is actually plotted. **Output content is unchanged**; only the tag/label are corrected. Panels exported before today under a `_cperr` name must be re-exported or re-labelled.
**Why (the question that surfaced it):** user asked whether the earlier trial-vs-trial-avg analyses used `L1DEVz`. **They do not.** `motion_analysis.m` / `prestim_variance.m` use `|Peak_imp − mean(Peak_imp)|` — a single PEAK scalar's deviation from the amp-mean peak, on the **ACTUAL** trace, in raw units. `L1DEVz` is `mean|r(t) − μ(t)|` over the whole dip window, on the **RESIDUAL**, z-scored within amplitude. Three differences at once (peak vs window-mean, Actual vs residual, raw vs z-within-amp), so numbers from the two streams are NOT comparable. Note `cp_agl.m` DOES use matched L1-dev across Actual/Global/Local, but normalises as a RATIO to the amp-mean (`x./mean(x)`) rather than z-within-amp — rank-identical within an amplitude, different once pooled ACROSS amplitudes.
**Next:** decide whether `cperr` should be implemented (run `contra_prediction.m` in the chain so `imp.cp_err` exists) or retired as a dead option. Re-export 2F. Corroborating note for the existing PAPER.md ⚠ on 2G/2H: with the matched L1 DV, pre-stim variance gives ACTUAL ρ=+0.721 and GLOBAL ρ=+0.700 vs LOCAL +0.287 — the power confound at its most extreme, exactly as those panels were flagged.

### 2026-08-12 — ROOT CAUSE of "only 9 ridge sessions": the 60000-frame cap DECIMATES the spontaneous list, killing every catch window
**Changed/Found:** rebuilt the ridge model for all sessions and the four missing ones failed identically — `ctrl_ridge_path: only 0 admissible catch windows`. Cause: `ctrl_ols_spont.m:319` caps the spontaneous set with `frames = frames(round(linspace(1,numel(frames),maxFrm)))`, an **evenly spaced decimation**. Above the 60000 cap that leaves no two consecutive samples anywhere, and catch windows require a contiguous peri-stim-shaped run entirely inside the laser-off set — so zero are admissible. It failed on exactly the four sessions sitting at the cap (0212, 0224, 0226, AL_0039_0419, all reporting 60000 frames) and succeeded on all nine below it (14598–59189). **Fix:** `ctrl_ridge_path` now takes `opts.spontMask`, and `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind` passes the UN-decimated laser-off mask rebuilt from the stim onsets via a new `local_spont_mask` helper replicating `ctrl_ols_spont`'s own rule. The ridge fit still uses the decimated `frames` through the Gram — only window admissibility needed contiguity, and contiguity is a property of the recording, not of the subsample. All four now build; the ridge set is **13 of 14** sessions.
**Why:** this had been an open question for two sessions of work ("why only 9?") and was unanswerable because the build log lived in a cleared workspace. It is a silent-truncation bug of the worst kind: the cap is a performance measure with no obvious connection to window contiguity, and the failure mode is total rather than degraded.
**Next:** AL_0039_0420_e2 (m13) is the one remaining failure and is unrelated — `data.dFk` is 91800 frames against 91875 in the SVD, a 75-frame gap that the ≤10-frame rounding tolerance rejects. Diagnose that separately; it has never had a Stage-2 cache in any mode.

### 2026-08-12 — ⚠⚠ BUG in the GLOBAL negative control: it used a MISMATCHED DV. Fixed — and it flips the MOTION verdict
**Changed/Found:** `utils/f2_state.m`. `local_globaldip` always returned the SIGNED dip mean, while the primary Local DV is `L1DEVz`, an UNSIGNED deviation from the amplitude mean. Those are different quantities, so "Local ρ vs Global ρ" was never a comparison — a signed level has no reason to track state the way an unsigned deviation does, which made **every** Global control look reassuringly small. Replaced with `local_compDV(tr, dcc, dv)`, computing the control with the SAME definition as `opt.dv` (L1DEVz / GAINz / DVz). Also added the **ACTUAL** (un-decomposed, trial vs trial-average) row using the same DV, because the ORDERING across Actual/Global/Local is the real result and Local alone cannot distinguish the two cases.
**AL_0033 e1, matched L1 DV, partial Spearman on `dev_pre` (n=748):**
| state | ACTUAL | LOCAL | GLOBAL | reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Motion | −0.154 | −0.099 (p=0.0067) | **−0.157** | Actual≈Global > Local ⇒ **GLOBAL effect, decomposition DILUTES it** |
| Rel-δ | +0.095 | **+0.114 (p=0.0018)** | +0.056 (ns) | Local > Actual > Global ⇒ **ENRICHED by decomposition** |
| Pre-var | +0.721 | +0.287 | +0.700 | confound, plainly global |
| Abs-δ | +0.674 | +0.241 | +0.639 | confound, plainly global |
**⚠ RETRACTION.** Earlier today I reported "Motion ρ=−0.099 vs GLOBAL −0.037, ~3× the control, which is the point in its favour." **That margin was an artifact of the mismatched DV.** With the control matched, GLOBAL (−0.157) is LARGER than LOCAL (−0.099) and `f2_state`'s own leakage warning now fires. The motion effect is NOT local. This independently agrees with `f2_state_var`, which flagged motion as leakage by a completely different route (BF p Local 0.0027 vs Global 0.0066; trend −0.80 vs −1.00). **Any Global-control number quoted before this fix is void**, including the GLOBAL columns of the 4-session pooled table logged earlier today.
**Why it matters for Fig 2:** the Actual/Global/Local ordering is now the decisive display. Rel-δ is the ONLY marker where the effect is larger in the residual than in the un-decomposed trial — the only one where the decomposition buys anything. That is the first genuinely independent support rel-δ has had, and it lands at the same moment motion (the fallback ending proposed earlier today) is eliminated.
**Next:** re-run every state number produced before this fix. Confirm whether `f2_state_var`'s GLOBAL control has the same mismatch (it uses the signed dip on BOTH sides there, so it is internally matched — verify).

### 2026-08-12 — "CL+preview makes trials more reference-SHAPED" tested eight ways and is false; the trade-off plane is the honest version, and it is strong
**Changed/Found:** Scratch probes. **Every shape-normalised metric names OL+preview, in 3/3 sessions** — per-trial Pearson r with the reference (pooled medians OL 0.253 / OL+p **0.438** / CL 0.366 / CL+p 0.351; OL+p-vs-CL+p p=0.001, CL-vs-CL+p **p=0.56 n.s.**), phase-tolerant max-xcorr (OL+p 3/3), |1−T| at 1 Hz (OL+p 3/3), error power at f0 (OL+p 3/3), ensemble coherence (OL+p or no separation), leave-one-out template correlation (CL+p is **worst** pooled, 0.360, p=0.005 vs OL+p), and across-trial dispersion of the z-scored trace (CL+p worst on s2/s3). The one absolute-units measure that favours CL+p, "time on target" (fraction of window within ±2 %ΔF/F), ranks it first pooled (0.393 vs CL 0.375, OL+p 0.343, OL 0.329) but **CL-vs-CL+p p=0.58, OL+p-vs-CL+p p=0.15** — only OL-vs-CL+p reaches p=0.044. **Root cause, and it is structural: "shape" means dividing out offset and amplitude, and the offset term is exactly where CL+preview's advantage lives** (lowest DC error in 3/3 sessions, and 40–65% of total error power sits there). A shape metric cannot show a feedback benefit — by construction. **The defensible panel is the trade-off plane**: x = |1−T| at 1 Hz (waveform fidelity, preview moves a mode left), y = across-trial variance (reproducibility, feedback moves it down). Mode means OL (0.990, 22.34) · OL+p (0.406, 23.51) · CL (0.678, 17.52) · CL+p (0.556, 16.25). **CL+preview DOMINATES plain CL on both axes, and OL is dominated by both closed-loop modes; only OL+p and CL+p are non-dominated — in all 3 sessions.** Draft panel built (5.4 × 5.0).
**Why:** user asked for a marker showing CL+preview squeezes trials into the reference's shape. It does not, and I stopped generating new metrics rather than continue until one favoured the preferred mode — eight framings with a consistent answer is a result, not a failure to find the right statistic.
**Next:** the trade-off plane gives the intended claim rigorously — *CL+preview is the only mode that is simultaneously close in waveform and reproducible, and it beats plain closed-loop on both counts* — without asserting it is best on any single axis (it is not: OL+preview is the more faithful tracker). If adopted, it replaces or joins 5H (4.2 × 5.4 slot is free) and the Results/Discussion text needs the "only mode to engage both mechanisms" sentence upgraded to the dominance statement.

### 2026-08-12 — CORRECTION to the 0212 diagnosis: the frame is rotated, and the real defect is that the midline bisects the LASER SPOT
**Changed/Found:** the earlier entry today claimed AL_0033_0212_e2's midline "splits A/P, not L/R". **That rationale was wrong and is retracted.** `cp_roi_masks` bisects by the signed cross product of the midline direction, so the split is orientation-agnostic — a rotated midline is legitimate when the session's imaging frame is itself rotated, and 0212's *laser-effect map* is visibly rotated ~90° relative to every other session (the cerebellar notch sits on the right edge instead of bottom-centre). So the 90° angle is a property of the data, not an error. Two things are nevertheless established: (1) swapping `bx`↔`by` takes 0212's midline 90°→0° and its outline aspect 1.07→0.93 (others 0.89–0.95), i.e. its stored geometry is a coordinate-order **transpose** relative to the other files — it and 0224 are the only two legacy ROIs with no `frame`/`view_used` field, predating the 2026-08-10 `native_rc` convention; (2) the decisive defect is that **its midline passes 2 px from the laser centroid** — drawn straight through the stimulated territory, so the laser centroid lands outside `ipsi_mask`. Every healthy session puts the laser 74–134 px from its midline.
**Why:** the angle test I first used is frame-dependent — it would fail any legitimately rotated session while passing a midline drawn through the spot. Distance from the laser centroid to the midline is frame-independent and separates 0212 (2 px) from all 13 others (≥74 px) with no overlap. The user spotted the transpose from the contact sheet.
**Next:** redraw 0212 (`XD_SESS=2; XD_REDRAW='all'`) with the midline clear of the spot; its Stage-2 R² = 0.855 is invalid until then.

### 2026-08-12 — Coherence at 1 Hz REJECTED as a Fig-5 panel; |1−T| at the drive frequency proposed instead
**Changed/Found:** Scratch probes (not committed). **(a) Coherence fails three ways.** Ensemble magnitude-squared coherence across trials at 1 Hz, γ² = |⟨YR*⟩|²/(⟨|Y|²⟩⟨|R|²⟩), with 2000-resample bootstrap CIs: s1 OL 0.54 / OL+p 0.71 / CL 0.72 / CL+p 0.64; s2 0.74 / 0.75 / 0.71 / 0.62; s3 0.69 / 0.75 / 0.57 / 0.59. CIs are ±0.10 and overlap almost completely, so nothing is separated; where an ordering exists it runs **against** the claim (**CL+p is lowest in 2/3 sessions**); and γ² is an SNR-at-f0 measure, so **CL is penalised for deliberately running a smaller-amplitude response** (|T| 0.70 vs OL's 1.08 on s2) rather than for tracking worse. Per-trial coherence at a single bin is not even defined (one trial, one frequency ⇒ γ² ≡ 1); the closest well-defined per-trial quantity, the R² of a 1 Hz sinusoid fit, gives the same non-result (medians 0.30/0.28/0.29/0.22 on s2, CL+p lowest). **(b) `|1 − T(jω₀)|` works.** T = Y(f₀)/R(f₀) per trial, so |1−T| = 0 is perfect tracking in both amplitude and phase; it is referenced to the REFERENCE rather than to the response's own power, which is exactly the confound that sinks coherence. Pooled over 3 sessions: **OL 0.974 (n=136) → OL+p 0.408 (110), p=6.8e-24; CL 0.673 (100) → CL+p 0.563 (132), p=0.0038; OL vs CL p=2.5e-11; OL+p vs CL+p p=4.1e-5.** Every pairwise contrast significant, ordering identical in 3/3 sessions. Two draft panels built: per-trial distribution (4.2 × 5.4) and the complex plane with distance-from-(1,0) as the error (4.6 × 4.6).
**Why:** user asked for a coherence-with-the-drive panel to support "CL+preview is best". Coherence cannot carry it, and would visibly contradict it; |1−T| is the standard control-theory statement of the same question and separates cleanly.
**Next:** ⚠ **|1−T| makes the same correction the phase data already made, but with far more power: OL+preview is the most accurate tracker at the drive frequency, not CL+preview** (0.408 vs 0.563, p=4.1e-5, 3/3 sessions). Combined with CL+p's phase overshoot (−9°/+4.6°/−24°, i.e. LEAD, where OL+p sits near 0°), the supportable claim is a **trade-off plus a design result: the fixed 5-sample lookahead is matched to the open-loop plant, so it overcorrects once feedback has already removed part of the lag.** A horizon scheduled on loop configuration is the fix. Do not write "CL+preview is best on all axes" — no mode is: at-f0 → OL+p (3/3), broadband/variance → CL (2/3), offset → CL+p (3/3), total error power → CL+p (2/3), per-trial RMSE median → CL (2/3).
**Also answered:** the dots in the draft error-decomposition panel are the **per-session totals** (summed bar height for s1/s2/s3), not per-segment values — ambiguous as drawn; either drop them or split them per segment if that panel is adopted.

### 2026-08-12 — 🔴 AL_0033_0212_e2's MIDLINE IS DRAWN HORIZONTALLY — its "contra" mask is the anterior half of the whole brain
**Changed/Found:** added a brain underlay to the kernel panel of `ctrl_fit_figs.m` (Stage-1 `ipsi_mask`/`contra_mask` as a truecolor background, ROI outline + midline over it, hemispheres labelled), and it exposed the bug on sight. Dumped `mx`/`my` from all 14 `cp_roi2_ctrl_*.mat`: **AL_0033_0212_e2 is (row 282, col 158) → (row 282, col 352)** — constant ROW, so the midline runs along columns and bisects the brain **anterior/posterior**. Every other session has a near-constant column (270–316) with the row sweeping 100→370, i.e. a proper left/right split. Consequence: 0212's "contra" grid is the anterior half of the *whole* brain and includes ipsi-hemisphere pixels, so its held-out R² = 0.855 is partly a same-hemisphere self-prediction, not a contralateral one — and 0212 is one of only **three** sessions clearing the 0.85 floor.
**Why:** the midline is what defines contra vs ipsi (`cp_roi_masks` bisects by the signed cross product of the midline direction), so a 90°-rotated midline silently redefines the entire model input while every downstream number keeps looking healthy. Nothing in the numeric pipeline could catch this — it took drawing the brain.

### 2026-08-12 — RETRACTED a circular exclusion reason; the one-session restriction re-justified on model quality alone
**Changed/Found:** `impulse-analysis/imp_fig2_state_0033.m` header rewritten. The earlier version justified dropping AL_0041 e2 partly because "rel-δ runs the WRONG WAY (ρ=−0.03)". **That is circular** — excluding a session because its outcome disagrees with the hypothesis guarantees the survivors agree, and is indefensible to a referee. Removed, with a standing note not to reinstate it. Also replaced the AL_0041 e1 justification: it had quoted the λ_R=0.3 UNGATED diagnostic (−0.076 dF/F, 11–22% of dip), which is not the model the pipeline runs.
**Correct per-session figures, from the pipeline itself under `F2_SELECT='r2max'`:** AL_0033 e1 — 748 trials, 6/9 amps, capture 91%, leak 9%, catch −2% → KEPT. AL_0041 e1 — 208 trials, 1/4 amps, capture 32%, leak 68%, **catch −21% ⇒ FAILS the 15% threshold, pipeline marks its capture/leak VOID** → hard exclusion. AL_0041 e2 — 260 trials, 3/6 amps, capture 37%, leak 63%, catch −14% (only just inside threshold) → weak model. AL_0048 e1 [R] — 300 trials, 3/3 amps, capture 29%, leak 71%, catch −8%, plus the 2.6 mm off-spot readout caveat.
**Why:** Every surviving exclusion is now decided by a criterion computed BEFORE any state test and blind to state markers, which is the only version that can be defended. The real discriminator turns out to be capture: 91% vs 29–37%. Leak 63–71% on the other three means the contra prediction absorbs most of the stim effect there, so their residual is largely not the local effect.
**Caveat that must be reported with any n=1 result:** AL_0033 is also by far the highest-powered session (748 trials vs 208/260/300; 9 amps vs 4/6/3). "The only session where the effect is measurable" cannot be distinguished from "the only session where the effect is real" with n=1, and it is one session from one mouse.
**Next:** If the Fig-2 ending rests on this, the honest framing is a single-session result with the power asymmetry stated, not a replicated finding. Check whether any additional AL_0033 impulse session exists that could serve as a within-mouse replicate.

### 2026-08-12 — Spectral probe: error power splits cleanly into offset / at-f0 / broadband, and it rewrites the CL+preview claim
**Changed/Found:** Scratch probe (not committed) — exact-4-cycle FFT of each trial's response and error over the 4 s window (dur×f0 = 4 cycles, so 1 Hz lands exactly on bin 5 at 0.25 Hz resolution; no windowing needed). By Parseval the per-trial error power **is** RMSE², so it can be split with nothing lost: **E@DC (offset) + E@f0 (gain/phase mismatch) + E_rest (broadband)**. Mean over the 3 sessions, (%ΔF/F)²: OL 10.97/3.14/10.55 (tot 24.67) · OL+p 13.13/**0.89**/10.04 (24.07) · CL 10.22/1.78/**6.62** (18.61) · CL+p **7.86**/1.22/7.72 (**16.80**). Best-per-session counts: **at f0 → OL+p 3/3**; **broadband → CL 2/3, CL+p 1/3**; **offset → CL+p 3/3**; **total → CL+p 2/3**. Also tested and REJECTED as markers: trial-to-trial phase-locking value (0.80–0.92, CL+p is *lowest* in 2 sessions) and f0's share of response AC power (12–30%, no consistent ordering). The plain response PSD is likewise a weak panel — the spectra are broadband-dominated and the four modes overlap almost everywhere except a small 1 Hz bump.
**Why:** user asked whether a power-spectrum analysis could show "how tight the controllers are at forcing the reference frequency", to support a claim that CL+preview wins on variance + RMSE + phase together. The decomposition answers it far better than a PSD, and it makes the mechanism explicit: **preview cuts the at-frequency error ~3× in 6/6 mode pairings; feedback cuts the broadband error in 3/3.** It also explains why plain RMSE hid both — **40–65% of total error power is the DC offset term**, which neither mechanism targets.
**Next:** ⚠ **the claim as stated does not hold and must be rewritten.** Phase: **OL+preview**, not CL+preview, has the smallest |lag| in all 3 sessions (−3.0/+6.9/−11.2° vs −4.8/−8.5/−25.0°) — CL+preview overshoots into lead. RMSE: CL is better on the *typical* trial (s2 median 2.80 vs 3.30) while CL+preview is better on the *mean* (Etot 14.12 vs 15.41) purely because its tail is smaller. The defensible version is: **CL+preview is the only mode that engages both mechanisms, giving the lowest total error power (2/3 sessions), the lowest offset error (3/3) and the tightest trial-to-trial spread — while OL+preview alone is the most phase-accurate and CL alone is the quietest.** Decide whether the decomposition becomes a panel in 5H's freed 4.2 × 5.4 slot.

### 2026-08-12 — ⚠ MY λ-SELECTION RULE WAS WRONG: it is minimised by the null model, so it shrank 5 of 9 sessions to nothing
**Changed/Found:** First ridge run produced ONE qualifying session, and the cause is a design error in `ctrl_ridge_path`, not the data. The rule was "smallest λ whose catch swing is within 10% of the swept MINIMUM". But the catch swing is the deflection of an operator whose weights are being shrunk toward zero — it decreases **monotonically to 0** as λ grows, because a null operator deflects by nothing. Its minimum therefore always sits at the top of the λ grid, and the rule selected the largest λ available. Evidence, from the 9 built sessions: **5 railed at λ = 10 (the grid maximum) with ‖b‖ ≈ 0.1–0.3 and R² collapsing to 0.43 / 0.46 / 0.62 / 0.69 / −2.07.** The three sessions that got a sensible λ (0.02–0.05, R² 0.813 / 0.815 / 0.908) got there only because `catch_falls` came back FALSE and my *fallback* rule ran instead — the fallback was doing the right thing and the primary rule was the bug. **A criterion minimised by the trivial model cannot select a model.** Corrected: λ is now the LARGEST value whose held-out R² is within `tol_r2` (0.02) of its own maximum — most shrinkage, hence least leak, for a bounded prediction cost, which is what the impulse-side result actually said ("4% of prediction amplitude buys 13× leak reduction"). The catch swing is now REPORTED at the chosen λ rather than optimised, `catch_falls` stays as the diagnostic for whether shrinkage bought anything, and a new `at_edge` flag fires when λ* lands on either end of the grid — i.e. when the grid chose it rather than the data. That flag is what would have caught this within one run.
**Why:** The rule was written from the impulse-side phrase "shrink until the spurious deflection stops falling" without checking that the quantity has a non-trivial stationary point. It does not.
**Next:** Re-run the ridge build. ⚠ Under the OLD rule every cached ridge number is void — `AL_0033_0304_e1` R² 0.447, `AL_0039_0420_e1` 0.455 and the rest of the λ=10 group are reporting a crushed model, not a model of that session. The one number that survives is `AL_0039_0430_e3` (λ=0.046, R² 0.851→**0.908**), which is the first evidence on controller data that shrinkage can lift held-out R² above the rank model's.

### 2026-08-12 — ⭐ NEW predictor model: whole grid + stim-blind shrinkage, as a REVERSIBLE alternative to pixel selection
**Changed/Found:** New `utils/ctrl_ridge_path.m` + `utils/ctrl_pred_tag.m`; `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind.m` gains a `CTRL_PRED` switch ('rank' = the old model, DEFAULT and byte-identical; 'ridge' = the new one). **The model.** Keep every contra pixel, shrink the weights, and choose the shrinkage from **catch windows** — peri-stim-shaped windows drawn entirely from laser-off frames, run through the identical operator and baselined identically. Under a perfect operator a catch window yields zero deflection; what it yields in practice is the operator's own spurious swing, and λ is taken where that swing stops falling. **Held-out R² cannot pick λ** (it maximises at λ≈0, i.e. it is blind to exactly what λ is for), and the catch rule never touches a stim trial, so it delivers the same property pixel-dropping existed to provide without needing a detector that can find anything. **Why the old model was the wrong lever, from THIS project's data:** the 2026-08-12 cache audit shows the three sessions whose selector stopped early (~100–150 of ~450 px) leak 14–17%, while every session pushed to the full grid chasing R² leaks 25–66% — i.e. K was acting as an uncalibrated, per-session regulariser via collinearity, which is precisely the mechanism the impulse stream identified (leak ∝ ‖b‖; ridge cut it 13× for a 4% amplitude cost, RESEARCH 2026-08-11). **REVERSIBILITY IS THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT** (user): the two models write to DIFFERENT caches (`ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind_<tag>.mat` vs `..._ridge_<tag>.mat`) via `ctrl_pred_tag`, so nothing the rank model produced is ever overwritten and reverting is one variable. All 10 scripts that read or write a Stage-2 cache were routed through that helper in the same pass — a ridge Global scored against a rank decomposition compares nothing, so mixing had to be made impossible rather than discouraged. `ctrl_ridge_path` returns the whole path (R², ‖b‖, catch swing vs λ) for the supplementary, plus `catch_falls`: ⚠ **the premise is not assumed** — a fixed λ_R=0.3 did NOT hold across impulse sessions (RESEARCH 2026-08-11), so λ is selected per session and any session where the catch swing does not fall is flagged and must not be called stim-blind.
**Why:** User asked for a better model than the current one, explicitly reversible. The audit had just shown the current one gates out 10 of 13 sessions with a floor calibrated against a ceiling (m4's 0.874) that no longer exists (m4 now reads 0.838), while simultaneously maximising leak on exactly the sessions it fails.
**Next:** **NOT RUN.** Run both modes and compare on the same axes: held-out R², leak, and the OL−CL rejection gain. Three outcomes worth naming in advance — (a) leak collapses and R² holds ⇒ adopt ridge, the floor stops binding and n rises; (b) leak collapses but R² falls below the floor ⇒ the floor itself is the next thing to settle, not the model; (c) `catch_falls` is false on several sessions ⇒ shrinkage buys no blindness there and the Fig-4 claim must rest on the OL-vs-CL ratio cancelling a common leak, not on blindness.

### 2026-08-12 — `ctrl_fit_figs.m`: the held-out prediction and the kernel, per session — neither had ever been drawn
**Changed/Found:** New `controller-analysis/ctrl_fit_figs.m` — one figure per session: (left) the held-out prediction against the actual ipsi trace over ~60 s of the test block, with R² and ρ; (right) the fitted weight map on the contra grid (the kernel) on a diverging scale centred at zero, with the laser site marked. Enabled by a new `[CTRL-OL-VAL]` block in `ctrl_ols_ol_stimblind.m` that caches the test-block actual/predicted (`OL.VAL`): **the held-out prediction had never been stored, only the R² it produces**, so "is this fit any good, or is R² carried by a few excursions" could not be answered without re-opening a 1–3.5 GB session. The figure script is read-only and mode-aware, so `rank` and `ridge` can be drawn and compared from caches alone. Sign is kept on the kernel map deliberately — which contra regions push the estimate up vs down is the interpretable part, and a one-sided colormap would hide it. Report block prints the R² and leak distributions and raises the `catch_falls` warning across sessions.
**Why:** User: "show me the pred and kernel for each session". Also the honest way to judge a new model against an old one — two scalars per session (R², leak) cannot distinguish a smooth distributed predictor from one leaning on a few extreme weights, and that distinction is exactly what the ridge-vs-rank choice is about.
**Next:** Sessions built before today have no `VAL` field and are skipped with a message naming the fix (rebuild). Run for `rank` first (the caches exist) to get the baseline picture, then for `ridge`.

### 2026-08-12 — BUG on first run of `run_fig4.m`: `load_sessions`'s `clearvars` destroyed the launcher's own config
**Changed/Found:** `run_fig4.m` failed immediately with `Unrecognized function or variable 'DO_REBUILD'` at the step-2 test. Cause: `run()` shares the caller's workspace, and `load_sessions.m` line 16 is `clearvars -except r_lean` — so step 1 wiped every variable the launcher had set, including its own CONFIG block, and the error surfaced one step later pointing at a line that was obviously fine. This is the **third** instance of the same trap in this file's history (`clear all` ate `r_lean` on 2026-08-05; `clear RB` ate pre-set `RB` config on 2026-08-12), so the fix is a naming contract rather than another one-off exception: `load_sessions.m` now does `clearvars -except r_lean RUN_*`, and every variable in `run_fig4.m` is namespaced `RUN_*` (`RUN_REBUILD`/`RUN_REJECT`/`RUN_MPC`/`RUN_FINAL`/`RUN_FRESH`/`RUN_HERE`/`RUN_FMT`). Nothing else in the project uses that prefix, so the exception cannot accidentally preserve stale analysis state. Both files carry the reasoning inline — `load_sessions` says why the wildcard exists, `run_fig4` says why its variables are named that way and to prefix any new knob. Code Analyzer clean (`load_sessions`'s remaining messages are all pre-existing, in the aggregation block).
**Why:** A launcher that a `clear` inside a called script can silently disarm is worse than no launcher — the failure mode is a plausible-looking error several steps from the real cause. Naming the contract makes it impossible to get wrong by adding a knob later.
**Next:** Re-run. If any other script in the chain is later given a `clear`/`clearvars`, it must carry the same `RUN_*` exception or the launcher breaks again the same way.

### 2026-08-12 — `run_fig4.m`: press-Run launcher for the whole Fig-4 controller stream
**Changed/Found:** New `controller-analysis/run_fig4.m` — one script, five steps: registry (`r_lean`) → `ctrl_residual_build` (Stage-2 rebuild, unattended) → `imp_reject_across_sessions` → `f4_reject_panels` → `ctrl_optimal_xsess`. Same interface as `impulse-analysis/run_fig2.m`: a CONFIG block of five flags at the top, nothing else to edit. `DO_REBUILD`/`DO_REJECT`/`DO_MPC` let any step be skipped once its caches are current (the rebuild is the only slow one), `FRESH_LOAD` re-reads the registry, and **`FMT_FINAL` drives the PNG-vs-PDF choice for BOTH panel scripts from one place** — `F4_FMT`/`OX_FMT` overrides were added to `f4_reject_panels.m` and `ctrl_optimal_xsess.m` so the launcher sets the format once and the two panel sets cannot end up in different formats. Every step re-entrant: each skips what it already has cached, so a crashed run resumes rather than restarting. Code Analyzer clean on all three files. **Same constant-folding trap hit a second time and worth recording as a pattern:** `if FMT_FINAL; FMT = {'pdf','png'}; else; FMT = {'png'}; end` is flagged as unreachable code, because `FMT_FINAL` is a literal in the CONFIG block directly above — the analyzer evaluates it and calls the other branch dead. Any if/else on a top-of-script config literal will do this; the fix both times was to index a cell (`FMT_OPTS{FMT_FINAL+1}`).
**Why:** User pushback — the run instructions had become a five-command sequence with a workspace flag to set beforehand, which is a worse interface than the project already has for the Fig-2 stream. The launcher is the interface; the ordering knowledge belongs in the file, not in a message.
**Next:** Run it. Step 2 is the only long one. If fewer than 2 sessions clear the R² floor, steps 3-5 assert by design — set `DO_REBUILD=false` afterwards so re-runs skip straight to the panels.

### 2026-08-12 — `ctrl_residual_build.m` gains `RB_*` caller overrides (its `clear RB` silently ate pre-set config)
**Changed/Found:** `controller-analysis/ctrl_residual_build.m` `[XRES-CFG]` now honours `RB_SESS` / `RB_REBUILD` / `RB_CONFIRM` / `RB_MODE` from the caller, mirroring `XB_SESS` in `imp_xsess_build.m`. **The bug this fixes is a silent one:** the CFG block opens with `clear RB; RB = struct();`, so the natural way to launch an unattended rebuild — setting `RB.rebuild = true; RB.confirm = false;` and then running the script — is wiped before the script ever reads it, and the run proceeds with the defaults (`rebuild=false` ⇒ every session skipped as already-cached, `confirm=true` ⇒ stops for a keypress). **Changed/Found:** User spec: each Fig-4 panel set needs **one single-session demo plus its own statistic**, with everything else combined across sessions, and **PNGs only until the layout is approved**, then PDFs off the approved code. ### 2026-08-12 — Cross-session MPC beat built: shared optimal-control kernel + `ctrl_optimal_xsess.m`, with the disturbance source made an explicit choice
**Changed/Found:** New `utils/ctrl_opt_solve.m` (the Stage-4b solve: plant → non-causal clairvoyant QP → causal receding-horizon MPC → the `frac_u0` accounting) and new `utils/ctrl_plant_markov.m` (delay-absorbed Markov parameters + Toeplitz `H`), both lifted verbatim out of `ctrl_optimal_control.m`, which now CALLS them — so the single-session workbench and the new batch cannot solve two different QPs, and `H` cannot be built three ways with three different delay conventions. New `controller-analysis/ctrl_optimal_xsess.m` runs the whole Stage-3 → Stage-4a → Stage-4b chain per session (Stage 3 and Stage 4a have only ever run on m4) and combines. `ctrl_ols_cl_deploy.m`, `ctrl_lti_sysid.m` and `ctrl_optimal_control.m` each gained a `CTRL_SELFIELD` caller override (same idiom as `XB_SESS` in `imp_xsess_build.m`) — without it a batch that sets `selField` has it silently overwritten by the stage script's own `selField = 4`, and every session would have been solved as m4. **The substantive design decision is the disturbance source, and it is now an explicit switch computed BOTH ways.** `'residual'` is what the m4 workbench has always used: `d = y_PI − H·u_PI`, measured from the PI trials, which absorbs plant mismatch — so the "optimal" controller is partly repairing the plant model and its advantage is flattered. `'global'` is the contra-predicted Global (`GgAbs`), the counterfactual no-laser ipsi trace: it carries no plant mismatch, and because it comes from the hemisphere that never sees the laser it is **available in real time**, which is what turns the ceiling from a bound into an implementable proposal. `[OPTX-COMPARE]` prints them side by side with the reading rule: a gap that survives under `'global'` is a control result, one that appears only under `'residual'` is the optimizer fixing the model. Outputs the three-way error budget per session — MPC gain / price of causality / irreducible — plus `frac_u0`, the fraction of the horizon where the clairvoyant optimum plays `u=0` because the disturbance already sits past the reference and one-sided actuation can do nothing. Four paperStyle panels to `paper/images/figure4/`. Same `ctrl_r2_floor` gate as the other cross-session scripts (under `'global'` it is not optional — the disturbance IS the predictor's output). All files Code Analyzer clean.
**Why:** User's Fig-4 story ends on "use this as a proposal for an MPC-type system — if we are given the disturbance ahead of time, look how much better it would do." The existing `ctrl_optimal_control.m` answers a related but weaker question, because its disturbance is a post-hoc residual rather than something a controller could ever have known. The contra-predicted Global is exactly the disturbance that IS knowable ahead of time, so it belongs in the comparison rather than being assumed equivalent.
**Next:** **NOT RUN** — blocked on the Stage-2 rebuild (`ctrl_residual_build.m`, auto-K), since Stage 3 needs it. Then run and check three things before any claim: (a) `plant_err` ≈ 0 per session (the `H` vs `lsim` sanity check — a nonzero value means the delay handling broke); (b) whether the `'global'` ceiling is anywhere near the `'residual'` ceiling, which is the whole credibility of the MPC argument; (c) `frac_u0` — if it is large, most of the "controller failure" is one-sided actuation and no design fixes it, which is a finding in its own right and changes what the MPC panel is allowed to claim. ⚠ Everything here is TRIAL-AVERAGED (y_PI, u_PI and Global are trial averages from the Stage-3 cache); a per-trial version is a strictly bigger claim and is not made.

### 2026-08-12 — ⭐ AL_0033-only state analysis + NEW variance test: Rel-δ passes the GLOBAL control on BOTH level and across-trial variance; Motion passes on level but FAILS it on variance
**Changed/Found:** NEW `utils/f2_state_var.m` (variance of the residual vs state: ACROSS-trial spread by state quantile bin as PRIMARY, Brown-Forsythe + monotone trend; WITHIN-trial roughness as secondary; `dev_pre` regressed out BEFORE any spread is measured; GLOBAL negative control on every quantity) and NEW driver `impulse-analysis/imp_fig2_state_0033.m` (AL_0033 e1 only, `F2_SELECT='r2max'` forced so the GLOBAL control is armed, `F2_BILATERAL=false`, knobs set explicitly so a stale `F2_*` cannot silently change the run).

### 2026-08-11 — ⚠ λ_R=0.3 does NOT hold up across sessions: capture is largely reporting CONTRA'S OWN response, and the catch control fails on AL_0041 e1
**Changed/Found:** NEW scratch driver `f2_pred_allsess.m` — per-amp trial-averaged Actual/Predicted/Residual at λ_R = 0 vs 0.3, ungated pixel set, run on all 4 registered sessions (AL_0033 e1 9 amps, AL_0041 e1 4, AL_0041 e2 6, AL_0048 e1[R] 3; 20 amps with a real dip, `A_dip < −0.2`).
(1) **λ_R = 0 fails universally** — capture median **8%**, range −2…33%, every session. The prediction lies on top of Actual at every amplitude and the residual is flat. This is a solid, session-invariant negative: the unregularised ungated model is unusable.
(2) **λ_R = 0.3 is NOT stable** — capture median 75% but range **16…136%** across the 20 amps. Values above 100% mean the residual is DEEPER than the actual dip, i.e. the model predicts an UPWARD deflection during the dip window and the subtraction over-corrects.
(3) **Mechanism confirmed quantitatively:** contra's own dip-window mean deflection `mean(e)` flips sign with amplitude, and with the near-uniform-positive weights the prediction inherits that sign. Predicted overshoot `−mean(e)/A_dip` vs measured `(capture − 100%)`: **Pearson r = 0.755, p = 1.2e−4; Spearman 0.723, p = 4.6e−4, n = 20.** ⇒ capture is substantially a readout of CONTRA'S response, not of the model's blindness.
(4) **CATCH negative control FAILS on AL_0041 e1** at λ_R=0.3: residual **−0.0764 dF/F with the SAME SIGN as the dip**, = 11–22% of that session's dips, so part of its "capture" is manufactured at 0 V. The other three sessions have opposite-sign (conservative) catch residuals: e2 +0.0666 (−27…−4%), AL_0033 +0.0551 (−9…−2%), AL_0048 +0.0145 (−2…−1%).
(5) **A "contra-quiet amplitude" filter narrows but does not rescue.** |mean(e)| < 0.03 → 6 amps / 3 sessions, capture 60–123%, median unchanged at 75%. |mean(e)| < 0.01 → only **2 amps in 2 sessions** (AL_0041 e2 2.70 V 60%, AL_0048 1.00 V 63%). Threshold is post hoc.
**Why:** Run to judge λ_R=0.3 before adopting it. It does not survive. The deeper point the sweep exposes: **contra is not stim-free at most amplitudes in any session** — so a predictor cannot be simultaneously a good spont predictor AND blind to the stim, except at the few amplitudes where contra genuinely does not respond. That is the actual blocker for the Fig-2 local-only claim, and it is physiology, not a detector or optimiser defect.
**Next:** (a) replace the post-hoc |mean(e)| threshold with a calibrated test of `mean(e)` against the catch null (same bootstrap machinery as `f2_affected_null`), giving a principled per-amp inclusion rule; (b) diagnose the AL_0041 e1 catch failure — a model that dips at 0 V invalidates every number from that session; (c) do NOT quote any capture figure, and do not adopt λ_R=0.3 as a fixed ridge. Model remains UNAPPROVED; `f2_model.m` defaults untouched (`F2_DETECTOR='tf'`, ridge unchanged).

### 2026-08-11 — ⭐ The leak is AMPLIFICATION, not contamination: it scales with ‖b‖, and ridge kills it 13× for a 4% amplitude cost
**Changed/Found:** Diagnostic sweep on AL_0033 e3 (442 ungated px, distance prior `Γ`, held-out spont R²). Three measurements, taken together, overturn the working hypothesis that the Global leak comes from imperfectly-excluded stim-contaminated pixels.
(1) **Per-pixel effect is BELOW the trial-average noise floor.** Signed dip-window deflection per pixel vs the catch-derived floor (0.1091 SD at these trial counts): |effect|/noise = **0.98 / 0.29 / 0.69** at 1.10 / 3.20 / 4.90 V. Nothing is individually detectable, so no detector can find it — see the companion entry on `f2_affected_null.m`.
(2) **The leak is DISTRIBUTED, not focal — and the earlier "3 of 442 px" figure was a signed-cancellation artifact (RETRACTED).** Sorting the per-pixel contributions `bᵢeᵢ` by |·| and cumulating the SIGNED sum reached 90% of the Global dip in 6/24/2 px; cumulating the UNSIGNED share needs **245/233/263 of 442 px**. Individual contributions are far larger than their net sum and mostly cancel, so the signed `n90` is meaningless. Never quote a signed cumulative-share statistic again.
(3) **Leak magnitude is set by ‖b‖, and shrinkage is strongly DIFFERENTIAL.** Ridge sweep — ridge 0 → ‖b‖ 67.9, max|bᵢ| 14.9, leak **94%**; 0.1 → ‖b‖ 2.4, leak 12%; 0.3 → ‖b‖ 1.4, leak **7%**; 3 → ‖b‖ 0.5, leak 3%. Over that same span the prediction's spont amplitude barely moves: `std(Ĝ)/std(y)` = **0.997 → 0.960** and held-out spont R² 0.9962 → 0.9408. So a **4% loss of spont prediction amplitude buys a 13× reduction in stim leak.** CATCH control (identical operator, no stim present): spurious deflection 0.0650 → 0.0081 dF/F, i.e. ~1% of the −0.7…−2.0 dF/F dip at ridge 0.3.
**Why:** Mechanism: the stim signature `e_a` lives in the SMALL-eigenvalue, high-collinearity directions of the contra Gram matrix — nearly orthogonal to the dominant spont covariance structure. A variance-based prior therefore removes it almost for free. This also explains retroactively why the TF detector "worked" (76% vs 6% capture at r2max): dropping 351 px removes collinearity, which shrinks ‖b‖ — it was never about removing contaminated pixels. ⇒ **The detector is not the lever; the prior is.** And the distance prior is built from geometry + the contra Gram alone, so it delivers exactly the PARAMETER blindness the model needs (b fit with no stim data) rather than the OUTPUT blindness (`bᵀe_a≈0` imposed) that the leak-penalty frontier buys and that disarms the GLOBAL negative control.
**Next:** Ridge cannot be picked by held-out spont R² (that maximises at ridge≈0). Test the CATCH-FLOOR selection rule — shrink until the operator's spurious deflection on catch windows stops falling — which is fully stim-blind because catch windows contain no stim. Verify it lands on a comparable ridge in all 4 sessions before adopting it.

### 2026-08-11 — NEW detector `f2_affected_null.m` (calibrated catch null + BH-FDR): finds ZERO affected pixels — correctly
**Changed/Found:** NEW `utils/f2_affected_null.m` — additive second detector, `f2_affected` (biphasic-TF match at a hand-set `tf_sens`) kept as the default fallback. Per-pixel × per-amp test of the trial-averaged deflection against a MEASURED null: draw `n_a` catch windows, average and baseline them with the identical operator, repeat 1000×, one-sided p, Benjamini-Hochberg at `q`. Single knob `q` is a false-discovery rate, so it means the same thing in every session (unlike `tf_sens` 1.0–3.0). Reports `.pval .stat .nAffAtQ .monotonic`; monotonicity in amplitude is now a checked, reported property. Wired as `F2_DETECTOR='null'`; `'tf'` remains default.
**Result:** AL_0033 e3, q=0.05 → **0 affected px at all 9 amplitudes** (median p 0.107–0.931), monotonic YES, pooled unaffected 442/442 — while `f2_decomp` still reports 7% capture. Initially read as a broken statistic; it is not. The companion entry shows the per-pixel effect sits at 0.29–0.98× the trial-average noise floor, so "nothing detectable" is the correct answer, not a failure.
**Why:** Built to test the hypothesis that leak comes from imperfect pixel exclusion. It answers that question cleanly and in the negative, which is more useful than a detector tuned until it flags something. The statistic is a NORM over the response window on purpose — a signed window mean lets a biphasic response cancel to zero and pass.
**Next:** Window is still `P.scc` (full response, 30–36 frames); the biphasic response cancels and noise dilutes the norm (at 4.9 V the signed window mean is +0.038 SD and `mean(aAc(scc))` is −0.026 dF/F vs −1.972 over the dip window). Re-run on `P.dcc`, or as separate dip/rebound tests flagged by either — though given (1) above this is now expected to change the p-values without changing the verdict.

### 2026-08-11 — Subspace-blind model BUILT and run ungated: works, but is LESS efficient than the window-mean penalty it replaces
**Changed/Found:** NEW `utils/f2_subspace.m` (stacked normalised evoked trajectories → thin SVD → `V_k`), `utils/f2_frontier_sub.m` (Woodbury sweep, one Cholesky for the whole frontier, window-free capture `η=⟨α,g⟩/⟨α,α⟩`), `utils/f2_subfig.m` (viewer: spectrum, `k(ν)`, frontier, `V₁…V₄` mapped, pixel weight map, held-out whole-response decomposition). Wired as `select_mode='subspace'` with `F2_NU`/`F2_KMAX`/`F2_SVW`. AL_0033, ungated 442 px, rank sweep:

| k | spontR² | price | capVal | random | gap | decomp | catch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 (ν=.90) | 0.980 | .016 | −6% | +4% | −9 | −11% | **+20% FAIL** |
| 5 | 0.964 | .032 | +4% | +4% | 0 | −1% | **−45% FAIL** |
| 11 (ν=.99) | 0.909 | .087 | +48% | +5% | +44 | +55% | +2% |
| **20** | **0.876** | **.120** | **+68%** | **+5%** | **+62** | **+88%** | **+3%** |
| 40 | 0.854 | .142 | +69% | +7% | +62 | +92% | +6% |
| 160 | 0.791 | .205 | +71% | +20% | +51 | +93% | +3% |

Reference — the window-mean penalty it was meant to replace, rank 6, same 442 px: price **0.051**, capVal **+87%**, random +6% (gap +81), decomp +93%, catch +4%.
**Why:** Three results. (1) **ν=0.90 was a bad default** — k=3 spans 92% of stim energy but the fit evades through the remaining 8%; capture goes NEGATIVE and the catch control FAILS at +20%. (2) **capVal plateaus at k≈20** (+68%) and buys only 3 more points out to k=160 while the price nearly doubles and the random control degrades 5%→20%. k=20 is the knee. (3) **The window-mean penalty is still better**: +87% for a price of 0.051, versus +68% for 0.120. The rank-6 `u_a = e_a/A_a` operator is a *directed* constraint — it targets exactly the reported quantity — whereas an orthonormal basis spans the response without knowing which combination matters, so it needs far more dimensions and each one costs R². Energy-weighting the basis (`sv_weight`) did not close the gap. The subspace version does deliver what it was built for — the rebound is inside `E_a`, and decomp capture reaches +88% — but it is not a free upgrade.
**Next:** USER DECISION. Either (a) keep the window-mean penalty and add a SECOND rank-n_A term built on the rebound window `rcc`, which keeps the directed form and its efficiency while fixing the rebound gap, or (b) keep the subspace and accept ~2.4× the R² price. My recommendation is (a). Also: I claimed ν would be a benign dimensionless knob, better than `tf_sens` — **that was over-sold**; ν 0.90→0.99 swings capVal −6%→+48%. The defensible knob is k, read off the plateau in the rank sweep, not ν.

### 2026-08-11 — CORRECTION: the TF detector is NOT a stim-independent guard, so the main argument for keeping it fails
**Changed/Found:** Earlier today's entry ("Dropping the TF detector…") closed with "dropping it means blindness rests entirely on the split-half + random control, with **no stim-independent guard**". That is wrong and the correction matters. `ols_tf_pipeline.m:643` prints what the detector actually does: `[AFFECT-TF] biphasic (inhib->rebound) TF fit | win 0..X ms (ref Y V) | dip-cap 0..Z ms | tf_sens=…` — it fits a biphasic TF **to the peri-stim evoked response** at a reference amplitude, then thresholds the fit quality at a hand-set `tf_sens`. It consumes stim data, and it has its own window parameters (`tf_win`, `tf_dipCapSec`). It is independent of the *fit*, not of the *stimulus*.
**Why:** The detector was being credited with providing an exclusion criterion that never sees the stim response — the one epistemic advantage that would justify keeping it despite costing ≤6 points of capture, a per-session hand-tuned knob, and non-monotonic per-amp counts in 3 of 4 sessions. It does not provide that. It applies a *different functional* (biphasic TF shape match) to the *same data* the penalty uses (evoked response magnitude and direction) — a second opinion, not an independent one. Under the proposed subspace model the redundancy is sharper still: `V_k` is an orthonormal basis built from the same evoked trajectories `E_a` that the detector fits and thresholds, so gating on the detector means pre-filtering with a lossy, hand-tuned reduction of the exact signal the penalty then uses in full.
**Next:** Do not spend interactive tuning passes on `tf_sens` across the four sessions. If a detector-like prior is wanted, fold TF-affectedness in as a CONTINUOUS multiplier on γ (no threshold, no clicker, no per-session number). Build the interactive viewer for the singular spectrum of `W` and the spatial maps of `V_1…V_k` instead — that is the object that actually enters the model.

### 2026-08-11 — ⚠ The TF detector's per-amp counts are NON-MONOTONIC in amplitude in 3 of 4 sessions
**Changed/Found:** Affected-pixel counts in order of increasing amplitude — AL_0033 `0 0 2 48 13 35 177 249 275` (48→13), AL_0041 e1 `30 21 74 15` (74→15, peak mid-range), AL_0041 e2 `0 0 0 73 4 198` (73→4), AL_0048 `0 68 121` (monotonic, and the only session at `tf_sens` 1.00). Monotonicity is a free, physics-based validity check the detector currently fails and that nothing in the pipeline tests.

### 2026-08-11 — The residual does NOT carry the rebound: blindness is enforced on the DIP window only
**Changed/Found:** Measured rebound capture (`100·Lreb/Areb`) against dip capture per session: AL_0033 **95% dip vs 37% rebound** (13–17% at 3.7–4.3 V), AL_0041 e1 55 vs 23, e2 69 vs 53, AL_0048 107 vs **−65**. Traced the cause in code: `rcc` — the data-driven per-amp rebound window — is built in `f2_prep.m:307` and read in `f2_decomp.m:45` **and nowhere else**. Every quantity that enforces or measures blindness (`local_dipvec` → `e_a`, the frontier penalty `Σ_a(bᵀu_a)²`, the greedy leak target, the ridge sweep's leak column) is defined on `dcc`, the DIP window. The predictor is dip-blind by construction and rebound-sighted by omission. Caveat on the numbers: only AL_0033 has interpretable rebound ratios — e1 and AL_0048 0.4 V have `Areb` ≈ 0 or wrong-signed, so their percentages are the same meaningless-ratio problem the dip analysis already guards against with `ampOK`, and there is no equivalent `rebOK` guard.
**Why:** The stream's headline is "the residual is the local stim effect", but the stim response is biphasic — suppression then rebound — and only the suppression half was ever made blind. AL_0048 is the informative case: `Greb` = 1.212 against `Areb` = 0.531 at 1.6 V, i.e. the contra prediction rebounds **more than twice as hard as the readout site does**. That is not Global absorbing a local effect; it is contra having its own larger rebound, which is direct evidence the rebound is a bilateral network event rather than local tissue recovering. Two further reasons point the same way: Stage 2's exclusion is driven by the TF detector's stim response, and a zero-lag linear map from a highly-correlated hemisphere preferentially captures slow distributed components — the rebound is slow (~0.3–0.8 s) where the dip is fast (~0.1–0.2 s).
**Next:** Run the frontier penalty on `rcc` (or on `dcc ∪ rcc`) and read the R² price, which separates omission from biology: if rebound capture rises cheaply it was an oversight, if it costs heavily or fails to transfer across trial halves the rebound is genuinely global. Add a `rebOK` response guard before quoting any rebound percentage. Until then do not describe the residual as "the local stim effect" without saying it means the suppression only.

Per-amp r is **too noisy to interpret** — the penalty operator is `Σ_a u_au_aᵀ`, so what must transfer is the SPAN, not each amp separately. Principal angles between the half-A and half-B subspaces give retained energy **0.52 / 0.41 / 0.44 / 0.42** — near-identical across all four, and far above the ~n_A/n_S ≈ 0.01 expected of unrelated subspaces.
**Why:** This REFUTES the explanation given for AL_0041 e1 ("the penalty silenced half-A noise; there is no stable direction to silence"). e1's dip subspace transfers as well as the sessions that gain. The surviving account is **evadability, not noise**: e1 pays an R² price of 0.0009 to reach `capSel` 98% — the constraint changed `b` without changing what `b` predicts. With 303 highly-correlated contra predictors the fit re-routes through equivalent pixels, satisfying `bᵀe_a = 0` while leaving the prediction, and therefore the half-B leak, untouched. The R² price is the diagnostic that actually separates the sessions: 0.069 / 0.0009 / 0.019 / 0.040 against capture gains +22 / +6 / +28 / +80. A constraint that costs nothing did not bite.
**Next:** The per-amp `r` print is misleading alone — replace the r<0.2 warning with subspace retention, or drop it. Separately, AL_0033 pays the HIGHEST price (0.069) for only +22 points and overshoots to 106%, so its frontier gain needs its own look before being quoted.

### 2026-08-11 — ⚠ The per-amp DATA-DRIVEN dip window biases the response test and inflates AL_0033 capture 84%→95%
**Changed/Found:** No code change yet — a confound found by reading `f2_agl_fig.m` output. `f2_prep` sets a data-driven dip window per amplitude, and its WIDTH runs inversely to amplitude: AL_0033 gets 34 / 17 / 15 frames at 0.5 / 1.1 / 1.6 V but only 9–12 at 2.1–4.9 V. Since `Adip = mean(trA(dc))`, a wide window dilutes a short dip, so weak amps are pushed under the `Adip < -2·sem` response threshold and dropped from the median. 1.1 V has a **peak of −1.75** and is labelled "no response" because its mean over 0–0.46 s is −0.706 against a −0.759 threshold. Re-scoring every session on the **canonical fixed 0–200 ms window** (the locked project decision, `peak_mode=3`): AL_0033 admits 8 amps instead of 6 and **median capture falls 95% → 84%**; the other three barely move (55→57, 69→73, 107→100). AL_0033 0.5 V also flips from a meaningless +0.076 to a real −0.378 (still sub-threshold).
**Why:** The response test and the capture ratio are both computed over the same per-amp window, so a window that widens when the response is weak biases in a single direction — it removes exactly the amplitudes whose windows it widened, and the survivors are the ones with the tightest windows. AL_0033 is the primary session and carries the headline, so an 11-point swing driven purely by window definition is not acceptable as an undeclared choice.
**Next:** USER DECISION — this touches a locked decision (0–200 ms inhibition energy). Either switch `f2_decomp` to the fixed 0–200 ms window for `Adip`/`Gdip`/`ampOK` and re-baseline every capture number, or keep the data-driven window and justify it explicitly. Do not quote 95% for AL_0033 until this is settled.

### 2026-08-11 — `f2_frontier.m`: constrained capture-vs-R² frontier; the R² price of blindness is ~0.02–0.07
**Changed/Found:** NEW `utils/f2_frontier.m` + section (d2) in `utils/f2_model.m` (`select_mode='frontier'`, `r2_floor`) + `F2_SELECT`/`F2_R2FLOOR` knobs in `imp_fig2.m`. Answers "maximise stim capture s.t. held-out spontaneous R² ≥ 0.85" as a closed-form **leak-penalty** sweep, not a pixel search: `(G + λ_R·diag(1/γ²) + λ_L·Σ_a u_au_aᵀ)b = c`, `u_a = e_a/A_a`, one solve per λ_L. Guards: dips used to SELECT come from trial-half A, capture REPORTED (`capVal`) is rescored on half B; random-direction control at the same penalty strength with matched column norms; catch control downstream. Result (knee pick, R²@λ=0 → R²@pick, held-out capture): **AL_0033** 0.931→0.862 buys 84→106% (random 84%); **AL_0041 e1** 0.980→0.979 buys 40→**46%** (random 40%) — FLAGGED, does not transfer; **AL_0041 e2** 0.947→0.928 buys 54→83% (random 56%); **AL_0048** 0.963→0.923 buys 34→**115%** (random 35%). Per-amp decomp capture 95 / 55 / 69 / 107%. **All four catch controls now clean, including AL_0041 e1 (−8%, was −21% under the R²-max weights).** Also fixed a column·row broadcasting bug in the weight-distance diagnostic that errored on every session.
**Why:** Under the R²-max rule capture tracked predictor count/location (91px→91%, 288–303px→29–37%), so the question was whether that deficit is *distributed coupling* (irreducible) or a *selectable direction*. The frontier prices it: in three of four sessions ≥80% of the deficit is removable for ≤0.04 R², and the random-direction control does NOT buy it — so it is stim-carrying structure, not shrinkage. AL_0041 e1 is the honest exception: capSel 98% vs capVal 46% means the penalty cancelled the trial-average dip it was shown, so its coupling genuinely is distributed at this SNR (1 responding amp of 4).
**Next:** `capVal` 106–115% on two sessions is **overshoot** — Global moves the wrong way on held-out trials — so the knee is still slightly too strong; consider picking the λ_L whose `capSel` first reaches ~95% rather than the 2%-of-max knee, and re-check whether the rel-δ pooled p (0.019 here vs 0.0025 under R²-max) is stable across that choice.

### 2026-08-11 — Frontier PICK rule: knee, not "strongest penalty meeting the floor" (the floor never binds)
**Changed/Found:** `utils/f2_frontier.m` — replaced `[~,j]=max(g(ok))` with the cheapest λ_L whose `capSel` is within `knee_tol`(2%) of the feasible max; added `GRID_EDGE` status + warning, `r2_price`/`cap_gain` outputs, and a >105% overshoot flag. The first sweep exposed why: in 3 of 4 sessions R² is still 0.92–0.98 at λ_L = 1e4, so the 0.85 floor is slack and the max-λ rule walked to the grid edge.
**Why:** At λ_L→∞ the penalty becomes the exact equality `b'e_a = 0` — the retired §17b NATIVE constraint, which always succeeds and so pins `capSel` at 100% by construction, carrying no information. The knee keeps the pick off that degenerate limit; selection still uses `capSel` only, so `capVal` stays a genuine held-out number. Moved AL_0048 from λ=1e4 to λ=2.15 and AL_0041 e1/e2 to λ=0.215 with essentially unchanged capVal.
**Next:** none.

### 2026-08-11 — DIAGNOSIS from the fit figures: the predictors are EXCELLENT and three of four are NOT stim-blind; capture tracks predictor COUNT and LOCATION
**Changed/Found:** With the fits finally visible, the two questions separate cleanly. (a) As PREDICTORS all four are strong: held-out spont R² 0.931 / 0.980 / 0.947 / 0.963, pred-vs-actual slope 0.936 / 0.978 / 0.922 / 0.976 (≈1, so no gain error the R² was forgiving), the prediction tracks the actual trace sample-by-sample rather than only its envelope, and the time-shift null collapses to −0.88…−1.13. Nothing is wrong with the regression. (b) As STIM-BLIND models three of four fail, and the weight maps say why. Capture is an almost monotone function of how many pixels survived the detector: **91 px → 91% capture (AL_0033), 229 px → 37%, 288 px → 29%, 303 px → 32%.** AL_0033's survivors sit in a thin anterior-lateral rim FAR from the midline; the other three keep predictors spread over the whole contra hemisphere including pixels adjacent to the midline, and in their per-amp panels the red (Global) trace sits almost on top of the black (Actual) — i.e. the "stim-blind" predictor reproduces the dip. The upstream cause is the detector: AL_0033 excluded 79% of the grid (tf_sens 2.15, 275/442 affected at 4.9 V), the others excluded only 30–47%.
**Why:** This reframes the whole question. The earlier reading ("the OLS is broken") is wrong — the fit is fine. What varies across sessions is not model quality but how much stim-carrying contra territory the detector removed, and `ridge=0` (picked by max R², per the user's criterion) leaves the soft distance prior switched OFF, so nothing else keeps near-midline pixels out.
**Next:** Test a HARD, pre-registered geometric exclusion (drop predictors within a fixed distance of the midline / site) instead of the soft distance prior. It is a criterion formed without reference to the dip, so leak stays an honest measurement, and unlike `tf_sens` it is identical across sessions — which is exactly what the current heterogeneity is missing. Compare capture and spont R² before/after on all four.

### 2026-08-11 — Two MATLAB traps hit while wiring the investigator (recorded so they are not re-hit)
**Changed/Found:** (1) `struct('sess', SS)` where `SS` is a struct ARRAY, and `struct('f', c)` where `c` is a cell, both DISTRIBUTE into a struct array rather than storing the value in a field — so the inspector's `IX` would silently have become 1×4 with a scalar `.sess` each, and the click handler would have indexed junk without erroring. Fixed by assigning fields one at a time after `IX = struct()`. (2) `clear <var>` inside a script blinds MATLAB's Code Analyzer to everything after it ("statement cannot be reached"); `run_fig2.m` now empties with `= []` instead, which `imp_fig2`'s `isempty` test treats identically.
**Why:** Both fail SILENTLY into wrong indexing or lost static analysis rather than erroring, which is the expensive kind of bug.
**Next:** none.

### 2026-08-11 — The §17c0 regulariser pick was CIRCULAR; picking on spontaneous R² instead drops capture from ~88% to 29–91%
**Changed/Found:** `ols_tf_pipeline.m` §17c0 picks `select_ridge` by MINIMISING LEAK subject to an R² floor ([ols_tf_pipeline.m:1223](impulse-analysis/ols_tf_pipeline.m:1223)) and then reports leak as an "honest readout". `f2_model.m` picks it by MAXIMISING held-out SPONTANEOUS R² — a stim-free criterion that never sees the dip — so leak becomes a measurement. The sweep tables make the circularity visible: on every session R² falls monotonically as the prior strengthens while leak falls with it, so the leak-minimising rule always walks to the strongest prior. AL_0041 e1 is the clearest case — at ridge=3 it reads capture **147%** (Global goes the WRONG way) for spont R² 0.90, versus capture **38%** at the R²-max point (ridge=0, R² 0.980). At the R²-max pick, capture is **91% / 32% / 37% / 29%** (AL_0033 / AL_0041 e1 / e2 / AL_0048) — far below and far more heterogeneous than the pipeline's headline.
**Why:** You cannot tune a hyperparameter on the quantity you then report. This is the single biggest reason the previous capture numbers could not be trusted.
**Next:** Any pre-2026-08-11 capture/leak number from §17c0's auto-pick is NOT comparable to these. Decide which figure the paper quotes before drafting the Fig-2 caption.

### 2026-08-11 — CATCH-TRIAL control added; AL_0041 e1 FAILS it (−21%), the other three are clean
**Changed/Found:** `f2_decomp.m` runs the identical decomposition (same z-scoring, weights, baselining, dip window) on the session's 0 V catch trials, or on the pseudo-catch windows sampled from spontaneous gaps where the session has none. No stim is present, so the Local dip there must be ~0. Result as % of that session's median stim Local dip: AL_0033 **−2%** (true 0 V, n=196), AL_0041 e2 **−14%** (pseudo, n=259), AL_0048 **−8%** (pseudo, n=299) — all clean; **AL_0041 e1 −21%** (true 0 V, n=55) — FAILS, so its capture/leak numbers are artefacts of the decomposition and are void. A time-shift null was added alongside it (prediction scored against a circularly shifted ipsi target): −0.88 to −1.13 on all four, i.e. the spont R² is genuine zero-lag coupling, not slow shared structure/drift.
**Why:** Any predictor that systematically undershoots around an event manufactures a "Local dip" whether or not a stim occurred. This is the cheapest decisive test of "is the OLS broken" and it was absent from the stim-blind stream. Answer: NOT broken in the manufacturing sense on 3 of 4 sessions.
**Next:** AL_0041 e1 has only 55 catch trials (vs 196/259/299) — check whether the failure is small-n noise or a real event-locked bias before excluding the session.

### 2026-08-11 — Greedy blind-pixel search FAILS on all four sessions and does not beat random exclusion
**Changed/Found:** `f2_model.m` runs `imp_greedy_blind` at a 98%-of-full spont-R² floor (raised from 90%, since the user's criterion is R²). Every session returns **FAILED_R2**: no subset of the unaffected pixels is stim-blind at that floor. On all four the random-exclusion control matches or beats greedy's leak at the same drop count, so the search is losing predictors rather than finding stim-carrying ones. The pruned set is therefore NOT adopted — the model keeps the full unaffected set. This reproduces [CP-STIMAFF] (S14) in the new stream.

### 2026-08-11 — Two bugs found and fixed in the new stream: polluted capture median, and RNG-order-dependent controls
**Changed/Found:** (1) `capture% = Local/Actual` is a ratio, so at an amplitude with no response its denominator is noise — AL_0033's 0.5 V row read **−93%** purely because Actual was **+0.076**, and AL_0041 e1's 0.8 V row read **−515%**. `f2_decomp.m` now derives a no-stim noise scale from the single-trial catch dips and marks an amp as responding only if its trial-averaged Actual beats 2×SEM at that trial count; all rows are still printed, only the summary median is restricted. This moved AL_0033's headline from 76% to **91%** (6/9 amps responding). (2) Seeding only at the top of the driver made the split-half permutation and the random-exclusion control depend on how much RNG earlier stages had consumed — the same session reported different control values depending on whether the motion variant ran (e.g. AL_0033 random leak 1.146 vs 1.226). `f2_prep.m` and `f2_model.m` now seed locally; verified identical across runs with and without the variant.

### 2026-08-10 — Model H's joint (Omega, W, B) solve does NOT converge — freezing the node dynamics beats it, and the choice changes W by 10x
**Changed/Found:** User asked whether the heterogeneous node components are learned before the network or simultaneously with it. Currently **both**: stage 0 fits Omega from each node's measured on-site response (linear, data-driven), then stage 2 re-fits Omega **jointly** with W and B under L-BFGS. Added `freeze_omega` to `fit_oe` to test whether the sequencing matters, and the answer is that the joint stage is presently **broken**. Frozen-Omega is a *strict subset* of the joint parameter space, so a converged joint solve can never be worse — yet **cold-start joint lands at SSE 8571 against frozen's 5978, i.e. 43% WORSE**. Warm-starting the joint solve from the frozen solution gives **5447, better than both**, which confirms it is an optimisation failure rather than a modelling result. The failure direction is identifiable: it is the same **Omega ↔ (W, B) scale ambiguity** that makes a ridge on `‖W‖²` ill-posed (node i's kernel can be scaled by any c if row i of W and B are scaled by 1/c), so L-BFGS wanders along a flat valley instead of descending. **The choice is not a detail — it dominates the network estimate.** Off-diagonal `‖W‖` rms is **3.91 frozen against 0.339 joint, a 10× difference**, and the two W estimates correlate only **+0.13**. The node kernels also move substantially when W is free to reshape them: median corr(h_stage0, h_joint) = **+0.732**, with **35 of 42 nodes below 0.9** and one at **−0.877**, and the across-node spread in kernel peak time grows from 139 ms to 170 ms. **The underlying confound is real and is the temporal twin of the B-vs-W confound:** a slow response at node i can be explained either by node i's own slow kernel or by drive that left and came back through the network, and nothing in a one-shot fit separates them. Anchoring Omega on the on-site responses puts it on the most reliable part of the data (reliability 0.71–0.88, against 0.33–0.66 off-diagonal) but is not neutral — the on-site response itself contains recurrent contributions, so freezing attributes those to node dynamics by construction. All three fits still sit above the reliability ceiling, so this comparison is about identifiability and optimisation, not about which is true.
**Why:** the question decides what "the network" in this model even means. With W differing 10× between the two protocols, any statement about coupling strength is currently a statement about the fitting protocol.
**Next:** **Fix the scale invariance before running either protocol again** — normalise `‖Omega_i‖ = 1` INSIDE `simulate` (with Jacobian `(I − w w^T)/‖Omega‖` in the adjoint) rather than applying `_norm_sign` after the solve. That single change makes the joint problem well-posed, makes the ridge meaningful, and should remove the cold-start failure; it is the same fix both open issues need. Until it lands, use the frozen fit or warm-start the joint solve from it, and do not compare W magnitudes across protocols. Afterwards the frozen-vs-joint comparison becomes a real experiment worth reporting — with the caveat that it can only be run inside the reliability ceiling, i.e. on 2 mW or reliability-weighted.

### 2026-08-10 — AL_0048 site search is UNMASKED and ΔF/F-normalised — a mechanism that would put the site on a vessel, and it matches the open 2026-08-02 doubt
**Changed/Found:** User: "I think the stim site is wrong for AL_0048." Read the site code rather than the site value (MATLAB busy with the fresh run). Two weaknesses in the `SITE_MODE='response'` branch (`load_bilateral_impulse.m:183-185`), which is the DEFAULT and the one that produced the cached site: (1) **the search is over the ENTIRE frame** — `min(slope(:))` with no brain mask and no hemisphere constraint, so nothing prevents the site landing off-brain or in the wrong hemisphere. The `'calibrated'` branch at least boxes the search to ±SITE_RAD of the galvo spot; `'response'` has no bound at all. (2) **`slope` is divided PER PIXEL by `mimg_b`** (`./max(mimg_b(:),eps)`, elementwise — so it is a ΔF/F%, not a scalar normalisation). Dark pixels therefore have a near-zero denominator and get their slope amplified without limit, which biases the argmin toward **vessels and frame edges** — precisely the dark features. A `brainMask` (`mimg_b > 0.1*max`) IS computed in this same script ~85 lines later for `allExperiments`, and is never applied to the search. Together these are a concrete mechanism for the doubt already logged and never closed on 2026-08-02: *"the readout site sits immediately beside a prominent dark round feature in the mean image — confirm it is not a vessel."* `data/al0048_0715_site_check.png` shows a small pale ring sitting inside the inhibition blob on the RIGHT panel, consistent with that feature. NOTE this is a mechanism, not yet a demonstration — the cached pixel has not been re-derived under a mask, so it is not yet known whether the argmin actually sits on the vessel or merely near it.
**Why:** the ~2.6 mm anterior displacement is documented and survives (RESEARCH 2026-08-02), but "the focus is 2.6 mm anterior" and "the exact pixel we read out from is the right one" are different claims, and only the first has ever been checked. Every AL_0048 number in the impulse stream is read from this one pixel's kernel.
**Next:** ⚠ **The site is CACHED (`data/cp_stim_site_AL_0048_0715_e1_R.mat`) and is reloaded before any search runs — today's fresh run reuses it and no fix takes effect until that file is deleted.** Proposed repair, pending user decision because it changes which tissue the session reads out: apply `brainMask` AND a light spatial smooth to `slope` before the argmin, keep `SITE_MODE='response'`, then compare the new pixel with the cached one. If it moves off the pale ring and the dose-response survives, the 2026-08-02 item closes; if the dose-response only exists AT the ring, that is evidence the "anterior focus" was partly vascular and the session's role in the paper needs re-stating.

### 2026-08-10 — THE CEILING: the off-diagonal Green's function is only 33–66% reliable, and that caps every propagation claim on this session
**Changed/Found:** Split the 5200 onsets by trial parity, rebuilt the Green's function from each half independently (`hetgraph_oe.build_target_trials`, native 35 Hz, no interpolation), and correlated the halves. This is the measurement that should have been made before any model was fitted. **Split-half r, and the Spearman-Brown reliability of the 50-trial average it implies:**  1 mW on-site **r=0.554 → R=0.713**; 1 mW **off-diagonal r=0.201 → R=0.334**; 2 mW on-site r=0.782 → R=0.878; 2 mW **off-diagonal r=0.493 → R=0.660**. Off-diagonal PEAK maps — the quantity every propagation claim is actually read off — reliability **0.314 at 1 mW and 0.669 at 2 mW**. **The consequence is a hard ceiling on model fit: the best attainable corr(model, measured average) is √R, i.e. ≈0.58 for the 1 mW off-diagonal and ≈0.81 for 2 mW.** Against that, today's numbers sort themselves out immediately. The output-error joint fit reached off-diagonal peak r = **+0.813 pooled across both amplitudes, which is above the pooled ceiling** — so its apparent advantage over the pure-injection model is substantially noise absorption, and two other diagnostics agree: its in-sample SSE (5831) is well BELOW the trial-noise SS (12160, from the cached Hstd/ntri), and on a proper split-half train/test it scores **negative held-out VE at every ridge strength tried**. The pure-injection (W=0) fit at off-diagonal r = **+0.653** sits at or under the ceiling and is the credible one. **Also established: at this trial count the target is too noisy for split-half validation to discriminate models** — memorising the training half scores VE −0.227 on the held-out half, and the best possible predictor of one half from the other is a SHRUNK copy (0.3×), at VE +0.145. **The 1 mW condition is the weak link**: its off-diagonal is one-third reliable, i.e. two-thirds of what a model fits there is noise, while 2 mW is twice as reliable.
**Why:** the entire model programme is trying to decide how much of the off-diagonal response requires propagation. If that off-diagonal is only a third reliable at 1 mW, no estimator can settle the question there, and a fit that appears to succeed is fitting noise. This governs every claim in the thread and should have been the first measurement.
**Next:** **Quote model fits against √R, never against 1.0**, and report the ceiling beside every correlation from now on. Three concrete moves this licenses, in order of value: (1) **fit 2 mW only, or weight by reliability** — the 1 mW off-diagonal is mostly noise and is currently contributing half the residuals; (2) **cut parameters to match the information**: pool the amplitudes behind one scalar dose factor (the ratio is a measured 1.63×) instead of a full B column per (site, amp), which alone removes 1764 of ~5800 parameters; (3) consider a **low-rank W**, which both cuts parameters and asks a real question — whether the coupling is low-dimensional. Do NOT read the current joint-fit W. Longer term this is an argument for more trials per site if the grid is ever re-run.

### 2026-08-10 — `hetgraph_oe.py`: Model H refitted to the Green's function — off-diagonal r +0.031 → +0.653 (W=0) / +0.813 (joint), with verified analytic gradients
**Changed/Found:** New `bilateral/grid/hetgraph_oe.py` replaces Model H's one-step objective with **output error on the measured impulse response**: minimise Σ (y_model[t, i | impulse at (s,a)] − H[a,i,s,t])² over the full 0–0.7 s window, every stim site, both amplitudes, with W and B free and no topology imposed. No autodiff exists in this venv, so the gradient is hand-derived (adjoint recursion: state adjoint `A_t = g_t Ω + poles·A_{t+1}`, drive adjoint `λ_t = Σ_r A_t`, output adjoint `g_t = dL/dY_t + Wᵀλ_{t+1}`) and **verified exactly against finite differences on a small instance where the loss is O(1) — max error/gradient scale 1e-10 across all of Ω, W and B** (`--selftest`, wired into every run). Fitting is staged and the stages are the science: **stage 0** takes Ω from each node's measured on-site response (linear), **stage 1** fits B with **W pinned to zero — the pure-injection model, where nothing propagates** — and **stage 2** joins everything under L-BFGS. **Results against the one-step fit are not close: off-diagonal peak correlation +0.031 → +0.653 (pure injection) → +0.813 (joint); full-tensor r +0.887; VE 0.456 → 0.786.** So the model class was never the problem — the objective was, exactly as diagnosed. ⚠ **But see the ceiling entry above: the joint fit's margin over pure injection does not survive scrutiny and must not be quoted.** **Two real bugs found and fixed.** (1) **`hetgraph.green_check` compared two different clocks:** the cached H is interpolated onto a 70 Hz window (`cfg.FS_WIN`) while the model runs on the 35 Hz imaging clock, and the comparison was index-for-index, so 28.6 ms model frames were being matched against 14.3 ms data samples. Corrected (`step = fs_win/fs`), which moves the previously reported scores from +0.355/+0.077/+0.042 to **+0.401/+0.062/+0.031** — the bug was real but was NOT the cause of the failure, so the delta-collapse diagnosis stands. `build_target_trials` now bypasses the cached H entirely and trigger-averages from `grid_trials_2amp.npz` on the native clock, removing both the decimation and the fractional-vs-percent conversion from the path. (2) **The sign/scale normalisation was changing the model.** Rescaling node i's kernel by 1/sc_i must be undone in node i's drive, so W and B scale by `sc` on the ROW index only; the first version also divided W by `sc_j`, which is wrong because y_j is the model output and is invariant. It surfaced as the reported loss RISING from 9668 at 400 iterations to 2.0e4 at 4000 — something L-BFGS cannot do — and is now caught by an assertion that the reparameterisation is loss-preserving. **A third issue is unresolved and blocks the ridge path: `‖W‖²` is not invariant to that same scale ambiguity** (Ω can absorb any scaling of W), so a ridge on W penalises an arbitrary parameterisation. It needs `‖Ω_i‖ = 1` enforced *inside* the forward model rather than applied afterwards.
**Why:** the one-step objective rewards a delta-shaped kernel, which is exactly the degeneracy observed; the impulse response is what the experiment measures and is the only objective that penalises it.
**Next:** Fix the scale invariance (normalise Ω inside `simulate`, with the Jacobian `(I − ω̂ω̂ᵀ)/‖Ω‖` in the adjoint) before any regularised fit — until then the ridge path is meaningless and `--ridge` should not be used. Then re-run under the reliability-weighted objective from the entry above. L-BFGS was still iteration-limited at 6000, so convergence is also not established.
